title: Personal Checking: courtesy refund allowance and fee age window by tier
content:
## Scope

A courtesy refund is a goodwill refund of a fee that was correctly assessed on a Personal Checking account. Each tier sets how many courtesy fee refunds one customer may receive in a rolling 365-day window and how long after posting a fee remains eligible.

## Allowance by tier

| Tier | Most courtesy fee refunds per customer in any rolling 365-day window (count of refunded fees, across all of the customer's checking accounts) | Fee eligible while no more than this many calendar days have passed since it posted |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Student Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Everyday Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Interest Checking | 2 | 60 |
| Premier Checking | 3 | 90 |
| Private Client Checking | 6 | 120 |

## Notes on reading the table

- The allowance counts refunded fees, one per fee, across all of the customer's checking accounts together, not per account.
- The window column is a count of calendar days since the fee posted; a fee stays eligible while no more than that many days have passed.

## Worked comparisons (hypothetical customers)

**Case A**: a customer whose only account is Interest Checking has received one courtesy fee refund in the rolling window. The Interest Checking allowance is 2, so one refunded fee is below it.

**Case B**: a customer whose account is Everyday Checking has received one courtesy fee refund in the window. The Everyday Checking allowance is 1, so that customer has already reached it.

**Case C**: a fee on a Premier Checking account posted 75 calendar days ago. Premier Checking allows 90 days, so 75 days is within the window; on Access Checking, with 60 days, the same age would be outside it.
